title: Quasi-compact morphisms of algebraic spaces: affine tests and Zariski locality
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]; a morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback over every quasi-compact scheme has quasi-compact source. For any $f:X\to Y$, the following are equivalent: $f$ is quasi-compact; for every affine scheme $V\to Y$ the space $X\times_YV$ is quasi-compact; there is a covering of $Y$ by open subspaces $Y_a$ such that each $X\times_YY_a\to Y_a$ is quasi-compact. Quasi-compact morphisms are preserved by arbitrary algebraic-space base change. For a representable morphism this is equivalent to quasi-compactness of every scheme base change in the scheme sense (inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact).

proof.text: Write $Q(f)$ for the scheme-test definition in the statement and $A(f)$ for the affine-test condition. If $Q(f)$ holds, $A(f)$ follows because affine schemes are quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Conversely, assume $A(f)$ and take a quasi-compact scheme $T\to Y$. Affine opens form a basis [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], so a finite number $T_1,\ldots,T_n$ cover $T$. Each inclusion is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and each $P_j=X\times_YT_j$ has a surjective etale atlas $U_j\to P_j$ from a quasi-compact scheme, by $A(f)$ and the definition of quasi-compact space. For $P=X\times_YT$, fibre-product associativity identifies $P\times_TT_j$ with $P_j$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Apply [lem-trf-space-finite-qc-atlas-assembly] to $P\to T$, the finite etale cover $(T_j\to T)$, and these atlases. It supplies a quasi-compact scheme atlas of $P$. Thus $Q(f)$ holds. If $T$ is empty, use the empty finite cover, which the assembly lemma explicitly permits.

proof.text: Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces, and suppose $Q(f)$. For a quasi-compact scheme $T\to Y'$, the universal property of sheaf fibre products gives $(X\times_YY')\times_{Y'}T\simeq X\times_YT$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Explicitly, a section on a test scheme on the left consists of $(x,y',t)$ with $f(x)=g(y')$ and $y'$ equal to the image of $t$; deleting $y'$ gives the right-hand pair $(x,t)$, and inserting that image is inverse. The right-hand space is quasi-compact by $Q(f)$ applied to $T\to Y'\to Y$. This proves arbitrary algebraic-space base-change stability, with no hypothesis on $g$.

proof.text: If $Q(f)$ holds, step 2 shows that every restriction over an open subspace is quasi-compact; in particular the single open $Y$ gives the required cover. Conversely, let $(Y_a)$ be an open covering with quasi-compact restrictions and fix an affine scheme $V\to Y$. An open subspace is representable by open immersions [def-a1-space-open-subspace], so $V_a=V\times_YY_a$ are open subschemes of $V$. They cover $V$: on each scheme test their point images are inverse images of $|Y_a|$ [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Refine this open cover by affine opens using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], and take a finite subcover $V_1,\ldots,V_n$ since $V$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Each $V_j$ lies in some $V_{a(j)}$, hence its map factors through $Y_{a(j)}$. Its quasi-compactness and the assumed $Q(f|_{Y_{a(j)}})$ show that $X\times_YV_j$ is quasi-compact, using fibre-product associativity [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Choose quasi-compact scheme atlases of these spaces. The inclusions $V_j\to V$ are etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so [lem-trf-space-finite-qc-atlas-assembly] supplies a quasi-compact atlas of $X\times_YV$. This is $A(f)$, and step 1 gives $Q(f)$. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine or quasi-compact.

Finally let $f$ be representable, so for every scheme $T\to Y$ the space $P=X\times_YT$ is a scheme [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a scheme, quasi-compactness as an algebraic space agrees with quasi-compactness of its usual topological space: the equivalence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] says exactly that an etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme exists if and only if its point space is quasi-compact; for schemes this is the usual topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Suppose $Q(f)$. For each affine open $W\subseteq T$, $W$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $X\times_YW=P\times_TW$ is quasi-compact by $Q(f)$ and associativity [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Thus the inverse image of every affine open under $P\to T$ is quasi-compact, exactly the scheme condition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Conversely, if every such scheme projection $P\to T$ is quasi-compact, then for quasi-compact $T$ its inverse image of the quasi-compact open $T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open]. It is $P$ itself. The scheme/space equivalence just recalled proves $Q(f)$. This proves both directions without assuming the test scheme affine or separated.
